title: Data-locality impact assessment for enterprise onboarding
content:
Purpose:
This is an impact assessment and practical checklist for onboarding enterprise customers who require strict data locality. It is intended for solutions engineering, on-call SRE, and the private-deployments implementation squad. Focus: understand technical changes, operational runbooks, and compliance gaps when a customer requests region pinning or must-keep-data-in-region constraints.

Scope:
- Applies to Redwood Private deployments (VPC + on-prem) and Dedicated reserved clusters when customers request region residency guarantees.
- Includes control plane interactions, logging/audit path, backups, monitoring, and third-party integrations (KMS, SaaS connectors).
- Excludes application-level PII classification (assume customer provides classification).

Executive summary (short):
- Primary risk vectors: accidental cross-region routing (eg during failover), snapshot/backup replication, telemetry export, and multi-tenant control-plane metadata that leaks location.
- Strategy: combine strict routing+network ACLs + storage scoping + deployment-level flags + automated validation tests at provisioning time.
- Minimal acceptable guarantee for initial offering: region-pin for user payloads (active inference data + embeddings) and logs stored in-region for 90 days; control plane metadata may be replicated but must be encrypted and tagged.

Key design constraints and requirements:
- Customer asks typically: "Keep all inference data within EU" or "Data must never leave Germany". These vary by legal regime — treat as tiered requirements.
- We must account for: backups (snapshots), async analytics (batched event export), observability (traces/metrics), and support workflows (debug traces shared with Redwood).
- Constraints from infra: some external hosted components (billing, auth) live in global control plane; we need to enumerate what is allowed to be global and document exceptions per contract.

Residency enforcement model (recommended):
1) Tenant-level pinning flag at provisioning: region_code (e.g., eu-west-1, eu-central-1).
2) Request routing rule: policy layer in edge router that only forwards to nodes in region pool. Reject with 403 if no regional capacity and customer contract requires strict enforcement.
3) Storage policy: set S3/GCS buckets or on-prem object store scope to region; disallow cross-region replication via IAM policies and IaC enforcement.
4) Backup policy: snapshots are stored in-region; if cross-region replication used for DR, require explicit customer opt-in and cryptographic envelope with customer-owned KMS.
5) Telemetry: redact or keep telemetry in-region by default; export pipeline must explicitly tag tenant and obey export rules.
6) Support/Debugging: create a consent workflow to copy traces out-of-region when required for debugging; logged and manually approved.

Practical checklist for an onboarding run (annotated):
- Provision tenant with region_code: verify IaC template sets placement constraints. Owner: Solutions Eng (Marco). Due: provisioning day.
- Validate routing: run synthetic traffic that includes pinned headers and confirm path to region nodes only (traceroute + request-id). Owner: SRE (Samir).
- Storage scan: confirm buckets used by tenant have replication disabled and lifecycle rules scoped. Owner: Infra Eng (Evelyn).
- Snapshot test: create manual snapshot, assert location, attempt simulated restore to different region (must fail or be blocked). Owner: Release Eng (Jenna).
- Telemetry flow test: push logs and confirm export pipeline refuses to route them to non-regional sinks. Owner: Observability (TBD).
- Key management: ensure customer KMS integration (if requested) is used for all at-rest keys; test key rotation. Owner: Security Eng (Aisha).
- Control plane metadata assessment: produce list of metadata fields that will be replicated globally and present to legal. Owner: Product Ops.
- Customer acceptance test (CAT): checklist signoff with customer security contact. Owner: Solutions Eng.

Known edge cases and mitigations:
- Failover scenario: if regional cluster becomes unavailable, do not auto-failover to other regions unless customer has opted into DR. Present fail-open vs fail-closed contract choices.
- Autoscaling burst: burst capacity in nearby region — treat as explicit NO unless customer permitted. Alternative: pre-provision reserved burst capacity inside region.
- Third-party connectors (e.g., SaaS embeddings stores): block connectors that spill data unless deployed in-region.
- Developer convenience features (stack traces, REPL): restrict by role and region; add explicit "allow-debug-copy" request with audit trail.

Decision log samples (working entries):
- 2024-05-12: Decided to default to fail-closed for strict-residency contracts (Aisha). Rationale: regulatory risk outweighs availability loss for targeted customers.
- 2024-06-02: Agreed that control plane metadata may be encrypted and stored in global control plane but must be tagged and discoverable for deletion requests (Marco, Jenna).
- 2024-09-09: Exception policy created for GDPR DSAR flow that requires a support ticket and audit before moving data out for third-party processing (Legal + Product).

Open questions (TODO):
- Which minimal set of control-plane fields can be safely replicated without violating residency assurances? (owner: Product + Legal)
- How to measure and report "in-region residency" continuously to customers? SLA metric or periodic attestation? (owner: Observability)
- Cost model for reserving burst capacity vs offering cross-region burst for non-strict customers. (owner: Finance + Product)

Tests and validation (automation):
- Add unit tests for routing policy that assert tenant header -> regional backend mapping.
- Integration test in staging: deploy two tenants (one pinned, one global) and run chaos test that simulates node loss to validate fail-closed behavior.
- Weekly residency audit job: run a scanner that enumerates tenant artifacts and flags any cross-region artifacts.

Operational runbook (short):
- Incident: suspected residency breach -> immediately isolate tenant traffic, snapshot current infra state, create P1 ticket JIRA-OPS-XXXX, notify Legal.
- Mitigation: if breach due to replication, revoke replication IAM, rotate keys, and block further exports.
- Communication: notify customer within contract SLA window; prepare remediation plan and root cause timeline.

Appendix: quick reference - allowed exceptions (proposal)
- Billing metadata (customer id, usage totals) allowed in global control plane if encrypted; must not contain payload identifiers.
- Anonymized telemetry aggregates for platform health allowed cross-region for 30-day retention.
- Manual debug export allowed after documented customer approval and audit record.

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc is intentionally pragmatic and prescriptive. Please add technical gaps as comments inline in Confluence doc CONFLUENCE-1234 and reference this file during onboarding calls.
- Immediate next steps: convert checklist into a step in the onboarding playbook and add automated tests to the CI pipeline.

Unpolished bits / scratch area (do not delete):
- brainstorm: customer might want jurisdiction-specific encryption keys per dataset -> link to KMS pattern doc.
- todo: catalog all existing backups and their replication configs (Evelyn).
- slack threads: #private-deployments thread "eu residency ask - acme corp" contains customer email copy.
